an5.72:2.1: “And how has a mendicant lifted the cross-bar?
an5.72:2.2: It’s when a mendicant has given up ignorance, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
an5.72:2.3: That’s how a mendicant has lifted the cross-bar.
an5.72:3.1: And how has a mendicant filled in the moat?
an5.72:3.2: It’s when a mendicant has given up transmigrating through births in future lives, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
an5.72:3.3: That’s how a mendicant has filled in the moat.
an5.72:4.1: And how has a mendicant pulled up the pillar?
an5.72:4.2: It’s when a mendicant has given up craving, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
an5.72:4.3: That’s how a mendicant has pulled up the pillar.
an5.72:5.1: And how is a mendicant unimpeded?
an5.72:5.2: It’s when a mendicant has given up the five lower fetters, cut them off at the root, made them like a palm stump, obliterated them, so they’re unable to arise in the future.
an5.72:5.3: That’s how a mendicant is unimpeded.
an5.72:6.1: And how is a mendicant a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached?
an5.72:6.2: It’s when a mendicant has given up the conceit ‘I am’, cut it off at the root, made it like a palm stump, obliterated it, so it’s unable to arise in the future.
an5.72:6.3: That’s how a mendicant is a noble one with banner lowered and burden dropped, detached.”
